what_is_nps.title: What is the National Pension System (NPS)?
what_is_nps.body: The National Pension System (NPS) is a voluntary, defined contribution retirement savings scheme designed to enable subscribers to make optimum decisions for their future. It's regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

points.title: Tier-I Account
points.body: A mandatory retirement account with tax benefits. Withdrawals are restricted until age 60.

points.title: Tier-II Account
points.body: An optional, voluntary savings account with no withdrawal restrictions. Does not offer tax benefits on investment.

what_is_nps.footer: Your contributions are invested in a mix of assets (equity, corporate bonds, government securities) based on your choice.

tax_benefits.title: Tax Benefits of NPS
tax_benefits.intro: NPS offers significant tax advantages, making it an attractive retirement planning tool:
points: Section 80CCD(1): Deduction up to ₹1.5 lakh (part of 80C limit).
Section 80CCD(1B): Additional deduction of up to ₹50,000, over and above the 80C limit.
Section 80CCD(2): Deduction on employer's contribution (up to 10% of basic + DA).
Withdrawal: 60% of the corpus withdrawn at retirement is tax-free.

withdrawal.title: Withdrawal at Retirement (Age 60)
withdrawal.body: At age 60, you can withdraw up to 60% of the corpus as a tax-free lump sum. A minimum of 40% must be used to purchase an annuity, which will provide a monthly pension.

comparison.footer_note: To choose between NPS and PPF, consider your risk appetite and return expectations. Use our PPF Calculator for comparison.

faqs.question: Can I withdraw from my NPS Tier-I account before age 60?
faqs.answer: Partial withdrawal (up to 25% of your contribution) is allowed for specific purposes like higher education, medical emergencies, or home purchase, after 3 years of opening the account.

faqs.question: What is an annuity?
faqs.answer: An annuity is a financial product that provides a regular income (pension) in exchange for a lump-sum investment. In NPS, you must use at least 40% of your corpus to buy an annuity from an IRDAI-registered insurance company.

faqs.question: Can I choose how my NPS money is invested?
faqs.answer: Yes, NPS offers 'Active Choice' where you can decide the asset allocation mix between equity, corporate bonds, and government securities. Alternatively, you can opt for 'Auto Choice', which automatically rebalances your portfolio based on your age.

conclusion.title: Plan Your Retirement with Confidence
conclusion.body: NPS is a powerful, long-term tool for disciplined retirement savings. Its combination of market-linked growth, tax benefits, and a structured pension makes it an essential part of a modern financial plan. Use this calculator to visualize your retirement corpus and start planning today.
